standard_prerequisites.name: Lambda definability
standard_prerequisites.statement: A partial function is lambda definable when some lambda term reduces inputs in Church numeral form to the Church numeral of the output whenever the function is defined.
standard_prerequisites.use: F is the term that lambda defines f, and the constructed H must lambda define g (977-979).

standard_prerequisites.name: Fixpoint combinator
standard_prerequisites.statement: A lambda term Y with Y h reducing to a term that self-applies h, giving recursive self-reference in the untyped lambda calculus; the unit uses it as a standard tool.
standard_prerequisites.use: The search loop is obtained as (Y Search) so Search can call itself with an incremented y (984-986).

standard_prerequisites.name: Regular function
standard_prerequisites.statement: A partial function f is regular when for every input the set of y with f at y equal to zero is nonempty.
standard_prerequisites.use: Regularity guarantees the displayed search reaches the least witness, so the reduction chain ends at the numeral of g's value (991-995).

core_obligations: Assume F lambda defines the regular f (977-979).

Define Search, the self-referencing tester that returns y when f applied to the inputs at y is zero and otherwise recurses with y+1, and set H to the fixpoint expansion (Y Search) applied to F, the inputs and the numeral zero (981-987).
Verify the reduction behavior: (Y Search) F n1 ... nk m reduces to the numeral m when f is zero at m, and otherwise to the same term with m+1 (989-993).
Use regularity to conclude the chain from zero terminates at the least witness, so H reduces to the Church numeral of g at the inputs, which is lambda definability of g (993-995).

proof_roadmap.step: Exhibit the search term and the fixpoint term.
Verify the two reduction cases of the search loop.
Conclude by regularity that the loop finds the least zero.

difficulty_reason: The counted lemma is the author lemma at source lines 971-976: if f is regular and lambda definable then the function g defined by minimization over f is lambda definable. The author proof (977-995) exhibits the search term and the fixpoint term, then verifies the reduction behavior of the applied fixpoint combinator on numerals: it reduces to the numeral m when f is zero at m and otherwise to the same term with m+1, and regularity of f guarantees the search terminates at the least witness. Writing out the self-application loop and its reductions is real lambda-calculus work, and the fixpoint combinator is used as the unit's standard tool.
